Investigations/UCB-04

Browser forensics of UC Browser

Investigating browser activity, private browsing traces and residual digital artefacts in a controlled Windows environment.

01

Project introduction

Private browsing aims to leave less behind. This investigation ran normal and incognito sessions in UC Browser inside a controlled virtual machine, then looked for what remained on disk.

Academic case studyThe activity was scripted by the examiner, so what was done is known. The report does not claim every private action was reconstructed.
02

Investigation overview

Environment
Windows 10 virtual machine in Oracle VM VirtualBox
Configuration
8 GB RAM, four processor cores, 30 GB virtual hard drive
Browser
UC Browser, normal and incognito modes
Tools
FTK Imager, X-Ways, DB Browser for SQLite, Magnet AXIOM
89,345items analysed in AXIOM

12tables in the History database
03

Investigation objective

What browser activity, private-browsing traces and residual artefacts can be recovered from a controlled Windows environment?

04

Background and context

Chromium-style browsers keep history, cookies and cache in per-user folders. Even when history is cleared, fragments can remain in unallocated space. UC Browser keeps its data under the user's AppData folder, and several of its files are encrypted.

Confirmed visit or potential activity?

A confirmed visit is one the examiner can match to activity actually performed, such as a history row for a site that was opened. A potential or system-generated artefact is a record that implies web activity without showing that this user opened the page, such as a cached URL, an autofill suggestion or a background request. AXIOM's 323 potential browser activity items are of this second kind: the report notes these URLs were not visited in the virtual machine.

05

Evidence sources

  • The virtual machine's virtual disk, converted to a raw image.
  • The UC Browser History database and related folders under the user profile.
  • Microsoft Edge data, because Edge was used to download the UC Browser installer.

07

Acquisition methodology

The virtual disk was converted to a raw image with FTK Imager (File > Create Disk Image). The image was saved as a multi-segment raw set, and the first segment was loaded into X-Ways after a refined volume snapshot.

  1. Create VMVirtualBox, Windows 10.
  2. InstallWindows, then UC Browser.
  3. BrowseSeven sites in normal mode, one search in incognito.
  4. ImageFTK Imager to raw .dd.
  5. ExamineX-Ways, SQLite, AXIOM.
08

Examination and analysis

X-Ways search hits

Keyword searches for the visited sites found URL fragments in unstructured and unallocated space. Their file system fields were blank, which suggests data outside normal file structures.

SQLite History database

Cookies, bookmarks and login data are encrypted, so they could not be examined in SQLite.

Magnet AXIOM

AXIOM parsed search history, cookies, LNK files, cached records, potential browser activity and locally accessed files.

09

Findings

Confirmedverified directly in the investigation outputRecoveredartefact recovered from the evidencePotentialpresent but not shown to be user-initiatedInterpretationanalytical readingHypothesisworking idea, untestedLimitationconstraint on what can be claimed
  • RecoveredRecovered URL fragments. Google queries, video links and a download portal appeared in search hits, residual data from earlier activity.
  • ConfirmedSearch history. AXIOM showed searches for the sites the examiner had visited, with URLs and timestamps.
  • RecoveredCookies. 12 matching results out of 89,345 items, with names, expiry dates and host names.
  • ConfirmedExecution. A UC Browser LNK file with creation and access times showed the browser was installed and run.
  • PotentialPotential browser activity. 323 items, mostly cached URLs, autofill and background requests. They were not visits made in the virtual machine.
  • RecoveredCache and local files. Cached records and frequent access to files in the browser's own folder support active use.
  • RecoveredStorage location. Data was found under AppData\Local\UC Browser\User Data_*, which gives a target for future extraction.
  • HypothesisAn advert-style site. One entry, uc123.com, may be the site opened in incognito mode. The report does not confirm this.
ArtefactConfirmed visit?Reading
History row for a visited siteYesUser-initiated, matches the script
Search hit in unallocated spaceResidualShows earlier activity, source file unknown
Cookie recordResidualShows a site set a cookie
Potential browser activity (323)NoNot shown to be a visit in this VM

11

Limitations and challenges

  • LimitationNo embedded video. UC Browser could not play embedded YouTube video here, so live video could not be tested.
  • LimitationEncrypted files. Cookies, bookmarks and login data were encrypted in the History database folder.
  • LimitationPassword hashes. Some were found in AXIOM, and attempts to decrypt them failed.
  • LimitationPrivate browsing. The report shows traces remained after incognito use. It does not claim every private action was reconstructed.
12

Technical skills demonstrated

Virtual lab designDisk imagingSQLite examinationCarved URL analysisCookie and cache analysisArtefact classificationTool comparison
13

Final investigative takeaway

Private browsing reduces traces but leaves residue, and good analysis separates a confirmed visit from a potential artefact.

Knowing where UC Browser stores its data lets an examiner target the right files. The 323 potential activity items show why a tool's label is not the same as evidence of a user action.
